title: Calibration Sanity Driver & Bias Detection Harness for Quant Profiles
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: As we roll out FP8/INT8 quant profiles across model variants, we need an automated driver that validates per-profile calibration and surface-level bias/regression signals before promoting profiles into canary or production routes. This ticket builds a lightweight "sanity driver" that runs a curated reference prompt suite, targeted bias probes, and distribution-shift checks as part of our CI and Dedicated/Private deployment promotion pipelines.

Scope:
- Create an extensible harness that runs calibration checks (statistical bias, token agreement, top-k token distribution), and semantic accuracy checks (embedding similarity, answer equivalence) for a given model+quant profile pair.
- Integrate a small adversarial perturbation stage to detect brittle calibration cases (typos, paraphrase, truncation).
- Define pass/fail gating rules used by automated promotion: numeric thresholds + fuzzy heuristics (e.g., EMB_SIM > 0.92 AND top1-agreement > 91% for language models; or explicit tolerances for LLMs on instruction tasks).
- Emit structured telemetry (per-prompt metrics, profile-level summary) to Console and to a new CI artifact bucket.
- Add visualization dashboard with trend lines and a single-line verdict (PASS/WARN/FAIL) for each profile run.

Non-Goals:
- Replace in-depth evaluation suites (existing heavy golden-suite jobs still own full regression). This driver is for fast gating and spotting obvious regressions early.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We prefer token-agreement and embedding-similarity signals for speed; full-suite semantic evals remain asynchronous.
- Use streaming-friendly metric collectors that can early-stop once failures exceed a configurable budget to save CI cycles.
- Bias probes will be intentionally small but diverse; they should catch egregious divergences rather than comprehensive fairness audits.

Outputs:
- CI job definition in github actions and a release hook for Dedicated image promotion.
- Telemetry schema and Console dashboard.
- A short runbook for interpreting WARN vs FAIL and instructions for follow-ups (recalibrate, widen quant ranges, revert).
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs in <= 12 minutes on CI for small reference suite on a single CPU worker (or <4 minutes on a standard GPU CI image).
Produces per-prompt metrics: top1_agreement, top5_agreement, embedding_cosine, token_level_kl, perplexity_delta, and calibration_bias_score.

Configurable pass/fail gate with defaults documented: PASS if embedding_cosine >= 0.92 and top1_agreement >= 0.91 and calibration_bias_score <= 0.04; WARN if one metric marginally fails; FAIL otherwise.
CI integration causes profile promotion job to stop on FAIL and surface the Console dashboard link in the CI logs.
Telemetry emitted to Console with sample-size annotated and a simple trend visualization available under {Console}/QuantQuality/ENG-40821.
At least two PRs merged: harness code + CI pipeline; and dashboard + telemetry schema.

comments: 2025-02-18 Asha: Created ticket after quantization weekly. Immediate goal: fast gating for profile promotion. Linking design notes: https://confluence.company/quant/calib-driver

2025-02-20 Marco: Proposed metric set in doc; opted for embedding_cosine + topk_agreement + calibration_bias_score to balance speed and signal. See RFC: https://drive.company/quant/rfc-calib-driver-v1

2025-02-24 Lina: Spike complete — prototype harness runs locally; token-agreement calculation is cheap. Found a corner case where short prompts cause noisy embeddings; will add length-normalization step.

2025-02-26 QA: Ran prototype against INT8 profile for open-lm-7B; observed embedding_cosine drop to 0.87 for a single instruction subset — flagged as FAIL by current thresholds. Investigating whether calibration or quant params caused drift.

2025-02-27 Marco: Decided to implement an early-stop budget for CI (max 20 FAILing prompts to abort) to save compute. Also agreed to default conservative thresholds and make them profile-configurable.
